source_text: Ἁμαρτάνουσι δὲ οἱ λέγοντες τοῖς προτέροις ἀμείνονα δεδόσθαι βίον, καὶ οὐ συνιᾶσιν, ὅτι πάμπολυ διαφέρει σοφία τῆς τῶν χρημάτων περιουσίας· καὶ τοσοῦτόν ἐστι φανερωτέρα, ὅσον ἄργυρος λαμπρότερος φαίνεται τῆς ἑαυτοῦ σκιᾶς. Ζωὴ γὰρ ἀνθρώπου, οὐκ ἐξ ἐπικήρου πλούτου κτήσεως, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ σοφίας περιγίνεται. Τίς δὲ καὶ δυνήσεται, εἰπέ μοι, τὴν τοσαύτην καὶ οὕτω χρηστὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόνοιαν ἐξειπεῖν; ἢ τίς ἀνακαλέσασθαι τὰ δοκοῦντα παρημελῆσθαι ὑπὸ Θεοῦ δικαίως; Πράττων δὲ οὐκ ὀρθῶς πρότερον ἔγωγε κατενόησα τὰ σύμπαντα, καὶ δίκαιον ἐμμένοντα τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, καὶ μέχρι θανάτου μὴ ἐξιστάμενον, ἀλλὰ καὶ δι᾽ αὐτὴν ἐπιβουλευόμενον, καὶ ἀσεβῆ συναποθνήσκοντα τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κακίᾳ. Χρὴ δὲ δίκαιον ὄντα μὴ πάνυ τοιοῦτον εἶναι δοκεῖν, μηδὲ ἄγαν σοφὸν καὶ ὑπερμέτρως· ὅπως μή τι πταίσας, πολλαπλασίονα ἁμαρτήσῃ. Καὶ μὴ ἔσο τολμηρὸς καὶ προπετὴς, μή σε θάνατος ἁρπάσῃ ἄκαιρος. Μέγιστον δὲ ἀγαθὸν ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι Θεοῦ, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ ὄντα μηδὲν ἁμαρτάνειν. Τῶν γὰρ ἀμιάντων χειρὶ ἀνάγνῳ ψαύειν, μυσαρόν. Ὁ δὲ μετὰ φόβου Θεοῦ ὑπείκων ἅπαντα διαφεύγει τἀναντία. Σοφία δὲ βοηθείας, στίφους ἀνδρῶν τῶν δυνατωτάτων ἐν πόλει μείζονα δύναται, ἢ καὶ συγγινώσκει δικαίως πολλάκις τῶν δεόντων ἀποτυγχάνουσιν. Ἄπταιστος γάρ ἐστιν οὐδὲ εἷς. Ἀσεβῶν δὲ λόγοις, οὐδ᾽ ὁπωσοῦν τι χρὴ προσιέναι, ὅπως μὴ τῶν κατὰ σοῦ λόγων αὐτήκοος γενόμενος, ὥσπερ δούλου πονηροῦ φλυαρίας· ἔπειτα δηχθεὶς τὴν καρδίαν, ὕστερον ἐν πολλαῖς πράξεσιν εἰς τὸ ἀντικαταράσασθαι καὶ σὺ ἐκτραπῇς.
thought_title: The superiority of wisdom over wealth and the danger of extremes
orientation: Solomon continues his teaching, refuting the claim that past generations had a better life, showing that true life comes from wisdom not riches, and warning against excessive righteousness or wickedness.
pass_a_gloss: Those who say that a better life was given to the former ones err, and they do not understand that wisdom differs exceedingly from the surplus of riches; and it is so much more manifest, by how much silver appears brighter than its own shadow. For the life of a human being is preserved not from the chance acquisition of wealth but from wisdom. Who then will be able, tell me, to recount the so great and so benevolent providence of God? Or who can call back the things that seem to have been neglected by God justly? Doing not rightly before, I myself considered all things, and it is right for the one abiding in righteousness even to death not to stand aside, but also to be plotted against for its sake, and to die together with the impious one by his own wickedness. But it is necessary for a righteous one not to seem altogether such a one, nor excessively wise and beyond measure; lest having stumbled in something, he sin many times over. And do not become daring and rash, lest death seize you untimely. The greatest good is to lay hold of God, and while being in this to sin nothing. For to touch the pure hand to the impure is abominable. But the one yielding with fear of God escapes all the opposite things. But wisdom is able to help more than the support of the most powerful men in a city; or it even pardons justly many times those failing in the things that are necessary. For no one is unerring. But to the words of the impious, not in any way must one draw near, lest having become a hearer of the words against you, like the idle talk of a wicked slave; then having been stung in the heart, later in many deeds you also be turned to curse back.

lemmas.gloss: they err / they miss the mark
to recount fully / to tell out
to lay hold of / to take hold of
hearing for oneself / a direct hearer

choices.why: Glossary does not fix this term; 'surplus' captures the sense of 'περιουσία' as abundance beyond need, contrasting with wisdom.
In context of life and wisdom, 'survives' or 'is preserved' fits better than 'comes through' or 'remains'.
Compound verb with ἐξ- suggests thorough telling; 'recount' matches the sense of narrating God's providence.
Strong ritual-moral revulsion; 'filthy' is too physical, 'abominable' captures the religious weight.
Rare compound αὐτός + ἀκούω; means hearing for oneself, not at second hand; 'direct hearer' preserves the force.
In military/civic context 'στίφος' means a body of troops or support; 'support of the most powerful men' fits the contrast with wisdom's help.

pass_b_english: They are mistaken who say that life was better in former days, and they fail to understand how far wisdom surpasses a surplus of riches. It is as much more evident as silver appears brighter than its own shadow. For a human life is preserved not from acquiring perishable wealth, but from wisdom. Who, tell me, can recount fully the providence of God, so great and so kindly? Or who can call back the things that seem to have been neglected by God justly? Earlier, while acting wrongly, I observed everything: the just man holding to justice even to death, yet plotted against for it, and the godless man perishing in his own wickedness. A just man should not appear to be excessively so, nor excessively wise beyond measure, lest by some stumble he sin all the more greatly. And do not be reckless and headlong, lest untimely death seize you. The greatest good is to lay hold of God, and while doing so to commit no sin. For it is abominable to touch the pure with a defiled hand. But the one who yields with fear of God escapes every evil. Wisdom can do more to help than the support of the most powerful men in a city, and it justly makes allowance many times for those who fail in what is required. For not a single person is blameless. Nor should you pay any heed at all to the words of the godless, lest, hearing the words against you as a wicked slave's idle talk, then, stung at heart, you too turn in many deeds to curse back.

problems.why: ἐπίκηρος means perishable or liable to loss, not 'chance'. The claim is that wealth is transient, not that it is random.
problems.fix: not from acquiring perishable wealth, but from wisdom.

problems.quote: I myself did not previously consider all things rightly: the just man who holds to justice
problems.source_quote: Πράττων δὲ οὐκ ὀρθῶς πρότερον ἔγωγε κατενόησα τὰ σύμπαντα, καὶ δίκαιον ἐμμένοντα
problems.why: The participles are objects of 'I observed', but the English leaves them verbless and dangling. It also turns 'acting wrongly' into 'not considering rightly'. The sentence cannot be parsed.
problems.fix: Earlier, while acting wrongly, I observed everything: the just man holding to justice even to death, yet plotted against for it, and the godless man perishing in his own wickedness.

problems.quote: so that you do not become a direct hearer of the idle talk of a wicked slave against yourself. Stricken in heart, you might later turn in many actions to curse back in return.
problems.source_quote: ὅπως μὴ τῶν κατὰ σοῦ λόγων αὐτήκοος γενόμενος, ὥσπερ δούλου πονηροῦ φλυαρίας· ἔπειτα δηχθεὶς τὴν καρδίαν, ὕστερον ἐν πολλαῖς πράξεσιν εἰς τὸ ἀντικαταράσασθαι καὶ σὺ ἐκτραπῇς
problems.why: ὥσπερ is a simile; the purpose verb is ἐκτραπῇς, cursing back, and καὶ σύ is dropped.
problems.fix: lest, hearing the words against you as a wicked slave’s idle talk, then, stung at heart, you too turn in many deeds to curse back.
problems.ruling: ὅπως μὴ governs ἐκτραπῇς, but the English cuts it into a separate sentence, losing the negative purpose. It also drops the ὥσπερ simile and καὶ σύ ('you too').

The Greek participles are objects of κατενόησα (I observed); English left them verbless and misread Πράττων as 'consider'. Fixed to 'Earlier, while acting wrongly, I observed everything: the just man holding to justice even to death...'.

last_rejected.quote: For a human life is preserved not from acquiring perishable wealth, but from wisdom.
last_rejected.source_quote: Ζωὴ γὰρ ἀνθρώπου, οὐκ ἐξ ἐπικήρου πλούτου κτήσεως, ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ σοφίας περιγίνεται.
last_rejected.why: ἐκ marks the source life comes from; English “preserved from” means shielded against.
last_rejected.fix: For a human life comes not from acquiring perishable wealth, but from wisdom.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκ σοφίας περιγίνεται: 'comes about/is secured from wisdom'; 'preserved from' is somewhat ambiguous but within range, and context (not from wealth, but from wisdom) makes source reading clear.
